findings.title: Equal-order crypto providers are now chosen silently by classpath order
findings.description:
The previous `foundProviders.size() > 1` → `IllegalStateException` guard is gone. Detection now sorts by `order()` descending and takes the first element.

- **The tie:** `DefaultCryptoProvider`, `FIPS1402Provider` and `WildFlyElytronProvider` all return `200`. `Stream.sorted` is stable, so the winner among them is whatever `ServiceLoader` iterates first, i.e. classpath order.
- **The impact:** a deployment with both `keycloak-crypto-default` and `keycloak-crypto-fips1402` on the classpath used to fail at startup. It now boots with an arbitrary one, possibly non-FIPS, and the only trace is a `debug` line.
- **Where it applies:** the Quarkus server sets the provider explicitly (`KeycloakRecorder.java:214`), so this affects the `CryptoIntegration.init(...)` paths: adapters, testsuite, embedded use, and the new `AuthzClient.create`.
- **Suggested fix:** keep the fail-fast when the top two providers share the same `order()`, or at least log at `warn`. Only the 100-vs-200 fallback needs to be silent.

No test covers the new ordering behaviour.

findings.title: ECDSAAlgorithmTest never exercises P-384/P-521 signatures or the long-form DER length paths
findings.description:
The test generates one key pair with `KeyPairGenerator.getInstance("EC").genKeyPair()`, which uses the JDK default curve (P-256 or P-384 depending on JDK version, never P-521). That key is reused for ES256, ES384 and ES512.

- **Untested branches:** only a real P-521 signature produces a SEQUENCE body over 127 bytes. So `ASN1Encoder.writeLength` (`ASN1Encoder.java:67-79`) and the long-form branch of `ASN1Decoder.readLength` (`ASN1Decoder.java:137-164`) are never executed. These are the most error-prone parts of the new code.
- **Self-consistent assertion:** the only check is `rsConcat == rsConcat2` after RS→DER→RS through the same new code. A symmetric bug passes.
- **Silent truncation:** on a JDK whose default is P-384, the ES256 case truncates 48-byte r/s to 32 bytes in `integerToBytes` and still passes.

Suggested fix: generate keys per curve (`ECGenParameterSpec("secp256r1" / "secp384r1" / "secp521r1")`). Then assert the re-encoded DER verifies with `Signature.verify` against the public key, or equals the original JCA output. Negative tests for malformed DER are also missing.

findings.title: ASN1Decoder leaks unchecked exceptions and is lenient on malformed input
findings.description:
Several malformed inputs escape the declared `throws IOException` contract or are accepted:

- `readLength()` returns `-1` for indefinite length (`0x80`); `readInteger()` passes it to `read(length)`, so `new byte[-1]` throws `NegativeArraySizeException`.
- A zero-length INTEGER reaches `new BigInteger(new byte[0])` and throws `NumberFormatException`.
- `readSequence()` (lines 49-63) checks only the low 5 tag bits, so primitive `0x10` or other-class tags pass as SEQUENCE.
- `readSequence()` does not reject children that overrun the declared length, or trailing bytes.

Practical impact is low today. The only caller path is `ECDSASignatureSignerContext.sign`, which feeds locally produced JCA output and wraps `Exception`. The class should still reject these with `IOException`.

findings.title: Dead statements in concatenatedRSToASN1DER
findings.description: `ASN1Encoder.create().write(rBigInteger);` and `ASN1Encoder.create().write(sBigInteger);` build encoders whose results are discarded. The same work is redone at lines 117-121. Remove the two lines.

findings.title: `order()` added as an abstract method on a public SPI interface
findings.description: All four in-repo implementations are updated. Any out-of-tree `CryptoProvider` will fail to compile, or throw `AbstractMethodError` during the sort in `detectProvider`. A `default int order()` would avoid that. The literals `100` and `200` are repeated across four classes with no named constant explaining the tiers.

findings.title: Fallback provider fails with unhelpful "Not supported yet." messages
findings.description:
Most methods throw `UnsupportedOperationException("Not supported yet.")`. Core code reaches several of them, for example `AsymmetricSignatureVerifierContext.java:63` (`getSignature`), `AbstractJWKParser.java:95-98` and `PemUtils`.

Because this provider is now auto-selected when no full provider is present, a user hitting one of those paths gets a message with no hint to add `keycloak-crypto-default`. The message should name the operation and the remedy.

Separately, `getBouncyCastleProvider()` (lines 61-67) returns the default KeyStore's JCA provider, not BouncyCastle. This feeds `BouncyIntegration.PROVIDER` and deserves a comment explaining it.

findings.title: Minor style and logging nits
findings.description:
- `logger.debugf(builder.toString())` passes a dynamic string as a format string. Use `logger.debug(...)` or `debugf("Ignored crypto providers: %s", ...)`.
- The ignored-providers list ends with a trailing `", "` and concatenates inside `append`; `Collectors.joining(", ")` would be cleaner.
- `ASN1Encoder.java:42` uses `static public` instead of `public static`.
- Both ASN.1 classes have empty Javadoc and `public` methods on package-private classes.
- `authz/client/pom.xml:67-71` adds `hamcrest` as a test dependency, but the only test uses `org.junit.Assert` alone.

findings.title: ASN.1 encode/decode and R‖S conversion logic
findings.description:
The conversion mirrors the reference `BCECDSACryptoProvider.java:28-70`: a leading zero byte forces positive integers, and r/s are left-padded or sign-byte-stripped to `signLength / 2`. I also traced by hand:

- `ASN1Encoder.writeLength` emits correct short and long-form lengths.
- `ASN1Decoder.readNext`'s mark/reset/count bookkeeping returns each child TLV intact.
- The `length >= limit` bound holds for a maximum-size ES512 signature.

findings.title: AuthzClient initialisation and service registration
findings.description: The constructor is private (line 236) and every `create(...)` overload funnels through `create(Configuration)`, so `CryptoIntegration.init` always runs before use. `init` is idempotent under its double-checked lock. The `META-INF/services` entry names the correct class, and order `100` correctly yields to the `200` providers when one is present.
